questionText: When a government designates a virgin forest tract as an inviolate National Park, the 'Opportunity Cost' of that conservation decision represents:

options.text: The cost of building high-voltage electric perimeter fences
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: The monetary salary paid to national park forest guards
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: The forgone economic benefits that could have been generated if the land had been converted into commercial open-cast mining, timber logging, or agricultural estates
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Opportunity Cost in Forest Conservation.

options.text: The total tourist entry ticket revenue collected annually
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Environmental and Natural Resource Economics (Opportunity Cost in Forest Conservation):
The forgone economic benefits that could have been generated if the land had been converted into commercial open-cast mining, timber logging, or agricultural estates

Detailed Context:
Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone: by choosing conservation, society sacrifices the commercial revenue from mining or logging.
Hence Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText:

List I:
(A) Solar Photovoltaic (PV)
(B) Solar Thermal / CSP
(C) Wind Turbine Generator
(D) Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC)

List II:
(I) Direct solid-state conversion of photons to direct current electricity via semiconductor p-n junction
(II) Mirrors (heliostats / parabolic troughs) concentrate sunlight to heat thermal fluid, generating steam to drive a turbine
(III) Aerodynamic lift forces rotate air-foil blades, driving a gearbox and synchronous magnetic generator
(IV) Exploiting temperature difference (minimum 20 degrees Celsius) between warm surface seawater and cold deep ocean water to vaporize low-boiling fluid
